metadata.note: Every cell outcome is derived from a REAL on-chain outcome: reverts were captured (reason recorded) and state was read back. method='executed' means the malicious tx was actually sent and its outcome observed; method='reasoned' means the property is a structural absence (e.g. no recovery function) argued from the verified contract source, not a sent transaction.

impersonation.mechanism: onlyOwner(identity, msg.sender): every state-changer requires actor == identityOwner(identity)
impersonation.evidence: attacker setAttribute reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'DIDRegistry: unauthorized'"; attacker changeOwner reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'DIDRegistry: unauthorized'"

replay.mechanism: per-identity incrementing nonce in the signed-hash preimage; second submission recomputes with nonce+1 -> ecrecover != owner
replay.evidence: first setAttributeSigned ok=true; identical replay reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'DIDRegistry: invalid signature'". CAVEAT: signed hash binds contract address but NOT block.chainid -> cross-chain replay is possible (documented limitation of ERC-1056).

identity_theft.mechanism: address-bound identifier; controller transferable only via owner-authorised changeOwner. No token/approval transfer surface.
identity_theft.evidence: changeOwner by owner ok=true; identityOwner now 0x90F79bf6EB2c4f870365E785982E1f101E93b906 (== newOwner 0x90F79bf6EB2c4f870365E785982E1f101E93b906); attacker changeOwner already shown to revert. Identifier (the address) never changes; a stolen owner key can still seize control.

sybil.mechanism: no issuer gating; every Ethereum address is already a DID (zero-cost implicit creation)
sybil.evidence: attacker created 5/5 independent DIDs unchallenged. Identity creation is permissionless and effectively free.

recovery.mechanism: no recovery primitive; changeOwner requires the CURRENT owner key, so a lost/compromised key cannot be recovered
recovery.evidence: contract exposes no guardian/social-recovery function; compromised key = permanent loss of control.

privacy.mechanism: identifier is the Ethereum address; attributes are pubkeys/endpoints emitted as events; no VIN/PII field
privacy.evidence: contract has no VIN storage or getter; createIdentity emits only a Secp256k1 verification key. DID form is did:ethr:<chainId>:<address>.

impersonation.evidence: attacker mint reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with custom error 'AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount("0x3C44CdDdB6a900fa2b585dd299e03d12FA4293BC", "0xeefb95e842a3287179d933b4460be539a1d5af11aa8b325bb45c5c8dc92de4ed")'"

replay.mechanism: no contract-level signed meta-transaction; all ops are direct calls protected by the Ethereum tx nonce
replay.evidence: ERC-721 identity ops (mint/transfer) carry no in-contract signature to replay.

identity_theft.mechanism: identity == transferable NFT; transferFrom / approved-operator moves the whole identity (VIN + history follow the token)
identity_theft.evidence: transfer moved ownerOf to 0x90F79bf6EB2c4f870365E785982E1f101E93b906 while VIN stayed "1HGBH41JXMN109186"; approved operator then moved it again ok=true. A stolen key OR an approval grants full identity takeover; no owner-authorised gate beyond token control.

sybil.mechanism: identity minting gated by MANUFACTURER_ROLE; unprivileged attacker cannot create identities
sybil.evidence: attacker self-mint reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with custom error 'AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount("0x3C44CdDdB6a900fa2b585dd299e03d12FA4293BC", "0xeefb95e842a3287179d933b4460be539a1d5af11aa8b325bb45c5c8dc92de4ed")'". Sybil cost = manufacturer authorisation, not just gas.

recovery.mechanism: no key-recovery primitive; deactivateVehicle (admin) only flags metadata inactive and cannot reassign token ownership
recovery.evidence: a lost/stolen owner key cannot be recovered; the token (identity) stays with whoever holds it.

privacy.mechanism: no VIN hashing; plaintext VIN stored in tokenIdToVIN / vinToTokenId / vehicleMetadata and emitted in VehicleMinted
privacy.evidence: tokenIdToVIN(1) read back plaintext VIN "1HGBH41JXMN109186"; vehicleMetadata.vin = "1HGBH41JXMN109186". Full PII (make/model/year/color) also public.

impersonation.mechanism: require(msg.sender == _owner) on addKey / removeKey / transferOwnership / execute
impersonation.evidence: attacker addKey reverted: "Transaction reverted and Hardhat couldn't infer the reason."; attacker transferOwnership reverted: "Transaction reverted and Hardhat couldn't infer the reason."

replay.mechanism: no signed meta-transaction surface; direct owner calls only (Ethereum tx nonce)

identity_theft.mechanism: identity = a per-vehicle proxy-account contract; ownership transferable only via owner-authorised transferOwnership (no approval/operator surface)
identity_theft.evidence: transferOwnership by owner ok=true; owner() now 0x90F79bf6EB2c4f870365E785982E1f101E93b906. A stolen owner key can seize the contract; transferOwnership has no zero-address guard (bricking risk).

sybil.mechanism: permissionless per-identity contract deployment; the only Sybil barrier is deployment gas (~529k each)
sybil.evidence: attacker deployed 3/3 independent identity contracts with no authorisation. Cost-gated only, not issuer-gated.

recovery.mechanism: no recovery primitive (no guardian, no admin reassignment)
recovery.evidence: compromised owner key = permanent loss; renounceOwnership can even brick the identity.

privacy.evidence: contract stores Key{purpose,keyType,key} entries only; DID form is did:key:<chainId>:<proxyAddress>, no VIN.

impersonation.mechanism: addClaim onlyOwner + on-chain ecrecover: recovered signer must equal declared issuer (EIP-191, EIP-2 malleability guard)
impersonation.evidence: non-owner addClaim reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'ERC735: caller is not the owner'"; forged-issuer-signature addClaim reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'ERC735: invalid issuer signature'"

replay.mechanism: issuer signature binds address(this)+topic+data (blocks cross-identity replay) but has NO nonce/expiry/chainid; same-identity re-anchor is accepted (idempotent overwrite -> ClaimChanged)
replay.evidence: valid anchor ok=true; identical re-submission also ok=true (idempotent, keyed by (issuer,topic)). No replay protection primitive; harmless here only because re-adding overwrites in place. Signature is not chain-bound.

identity_theft.mechanism: identity = per-vehicle claim-holder contract; transferOwnership is onlyOwner (no approval/operator surface)
identity_theft.evidence: transferOwnership by owner ok=true. Stolen owner key can seize; no passive transfer surface.

sybil.mechanism: permissionless per-identity contract deployment; Sybil barrier is deployment gas only (~1.40M each — the most expensive to spam)
sybil.evidence: attacker deployed 3/3 claim-holder identities unchallenged. Cost-gated only; claims themselves still need a trusted issuer signature.

recovery.mechanism: no recovery primitive (owner is the sole MANAGEMENT key)
recovery.evidence: compromised owner key = permanent loss of the identity contract.

privacy.mechanism: constructor stores VIN as `string public vin` and emits VehicleIdentityCreated(vinHash, vin, owner) with plaintext VIN
privacy.evidence: holder.vin() read back plaintext "1HGBH41JXMN109186" (vinHash is also stored, but plaintext is exposed alongside it).

impersonation.evidence: attacker registerVehicle reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with custom error 'AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount("0x3C44CdDdB6a900fa2b585dd299e03d12FA4293BC", "0x114e74f6ea3bd819998f78687bfcb11b140da08e9b7d222fa9c1f1ba1f2aa122")'"

replay.mechanism: no signed meta-transaction surface; issuer-gated direct calls (Ethereum tx nonce)

identity_theft.mechanism: soulbound: _update blocks transfers between non-zero addresses unless msg.sender holds ISSUER_ROLE
identity_theft.evidence: holder safeTransferFrom of BIRTH_CERT reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'CVIN1155: credentials are soulbound (issuer-mediated transfer only)'". A stolen vehicle key cannot move the identity token; only an issuer can re-bind it.

sybil.evidence: attacker self-register reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with custom error 'AccessControlUnauthorizedAccount("0x3C44CdDdB6a900fa2b585dd299e03d12FA4293BC", "0x114e74f6ea3bd819998f78687bfcb11b140da08e9b7d222fa9c1f1ba1f2aa122")'". Sybil cost = issuer authorisation.

recovery.mechanism: issuer-mediated recovery: ISSUER_ROLE can issuerTransferCredential the BIRTH_CERT to a new vehicle address (re-binds VIN)
recovery.evidence: issuer re-bound identity to 0x90F79bf6EB2c4f870365E785982E1f101E93b906; balanceOf(new, BIRTH_CERT)=1. Recovery depends on a trusted issuer, not the key holder.

privacy.mechanism: no VIN hashing for storage; plaintext VIN in `vehicleVIN` mapping and VehicleRegistered(vehicle, vinHash, vin) event
privacy.evidence: vehicleVIN() read back plaintext "1HGBH41JXMN109186" (a keccak vinHash index also exists, but plaintext is stored+emitted).

impersonation.mechanism: onlyOwnerOrEntryPoint on direct calls; validateUserOp ecrecover requires recovered == owner (EntryPoint reverts on validationData != 0)
impersonation.evidence: direct attacker setAttribute reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'CVINVehicleAccount: not owner or entryPoint'"; attacker-signed UserOp reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'CVINEntryPoint: signature validation failed'"

replay.mechanism: EntryPoint enforces require(userOp.nonce == nonces[sender]) and bumps it; userOpHash also binds entryPoint address + block.chainid
replay.evidence: first handleOp ok=true; identical replay reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'CVINEntryPoint: invalid nonce'". Best replay posture (nonce + chainid-bound hash).

identity_theft.mechanism: identity = stable account address; only the owner signing key rotates via owner-authorised transferOwnership (no token/approval surface)
identity_theft.evidence: transferOwnership (key rotation) ok=true; account address (identity) unchanged. A stolen owner key can rotate itself out, but guardian recovery (below) can restore control.

sybil.mechanism: permissionless smart-account deployment; Sybil barrier is deployment gas only (~768k each)
sybil.evidence: attacker deployed 3/3 accounts unchallenged. Cost-gated only, not issuer-gated.

recovery.mechanism: guardian social recovery: recoverOwner(newOwner) callable only by the designated guardian installs a fresh signing key without changing the identity address
recovery.evidence: non-guardian recoverOwner reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'CVINVehicleAccount: not guardian'"; guardian recoverOwner ok=true; owner() now 0x15d34AAf54267DB7D7c367839AAf71A00a2C6A65 (== recovered 0x15d34AAf54267DB7D7c367839AAf71A00a2C6A65). CAVEAT: single-guardian, instant, no timelock/threshold -> a compromised guardian is itself a takeover vector.

privacy.mechanism: ERC-725Y-style attribute store is public and does NOT hash values; app-dependent (no forced VIN field, but any VIN written is exposed via getAttribute + AttributeChanged event)
privacy.evidence: setAttribute(vin) then getAttribute read back plaintext "1HGBH41JXMN109186". No built-in VIN protection; privacy depends on the application encrypting before storing.

identity_theft.mechanism: identity == transferable token; the token owner can move the whole identity via transfer (VIN data follows the tokenId)
identity_theft.evidence: token owner transfer ok=true, tokenOwnerOf now 0x90F79bf6EB2c4f870365E785982E1f101E93b906; non-owner transfer reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'LSP8: caller is not the token owner'". A stolen token-owner key = stolen identity (no operator surface, so slightly narrower than ERC-721, but still freely transferable by the holder).

sybil.mechanism: identity minting gated by the issuing authority (onlyOwner)
sybil.evidence: attacker self-mint reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'LSP8: caller is not the contract owner'". Sybil cost = authority authorisation.

recovery.mechanism: authority-mediated recovery: the issuing authority can revokeVehicle then re-mint the same tokenId (keccak256(VIN)) to a new owner
recovery.evidence: authority revoked + re-minted identity to a new owner ok=true. Recovery depends on a trusted authority, not the key holder.

privacy.mechanism: tokenId = keccak256(VIN) is hashed, but the plaintext VIN is also stored under DATA_KEY_VIN and emitted in TokenIdDataChanged / VehicleMinted

impersonation.mechanism: onlyAuthorizedManufacturer on registerVehicleBirth; recordLifecycleEvent gated by onlyAuthorizedIssuer(eventType) role matrix
impersonation.evidence: attacker registerVehicleBirth reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'Only authorized manufacturers can register vehicles'"

replay.mechanism: no signed meta-tx on the identity path (role-gated direct calls); attestEvent stores a signature blob that is NEVER verified on-chain (no ecrecover) — a replay/forgery gap for attestations
replay.evidence: birth/ownership ops carry no replayable in-contract signature; attestEvent signatures are unvalidated and could be replayed/forged (only gated by attester role).

identity_theft.mechanism: owner-authorised transferVehicleOwnership (onlyOwner(identity, actor)); immutable birth certificate + full ownership history preserve provenance across transfers
identity_theft.evidence: transferVehicleOwnership by owner ok=true; identityOwner now 0x90F79bf6EB2c4f870365E785982E1f101E93b906. A stolen owner key can transfer, but the birth cert and odometer-stamped ownership chain remain tamper-evident.

sybil.mechanism: identity creation gated by onlyAuthorizedManufacturer AND VIN-hash uniqueness; highest per-identity cost (~299k gas)
sybil.evidence: attacker registerVehicleBirth reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'Only authorized manufacturers can register vehicles'". Strongest Sybil resistance: manufacturer authorisation + unique-VIN enforcement.

recovery.mechanism: inherits ERC-1056 changeOwner (requires current owner key); no guardian/social recovery
recovery.evidence: a compromised owner key cannot be recovered by the vehicle; registryAuthority can re-authorize manufacturers but cannot restore a lost owner key.

privacy.mechanism: VIN stored ONLY as bytes32 vinHash + off-chain-encrypted `encryptedVIN`; VehicleBirthRegistered event emits the hash, not the VIN; DID is did:ethr:<chainId>:<address>
privacy.evidence: vehicleBirths.vinHash = 0x4033859e568c05f5545f080dd3e2646cc5056351fc2fe2dccdd0bad65ddb203d (hash); encryptedVIN = "encrypted:AES256:VINCIPHERTEXT==" (ciphertext, not the VIN); getVehicleDID() = "did:ethr:0x7a69:15d34aaf54267db7d7c367839aaf71a00a2c6a65" (no VIN in the DID). Only family that avoids plaintext VIN on-chain.

impersonation.mechanism: onlyIdentityOwner on ERC-1056 side; addClaim ecrecover requires recovered raw-digest signer == declared issuer
impersonation.evidence: attacker setAttribute reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'CVINCombined: unauthorized'"; forged-issuer claim reverted: "VM Exception while processing transaction: reverted with reason string 'CVINCombined: invalid claim signature'"

replay.mechanism: claim signature binds address(this)+identity+topic+data (blocks cross-context replay) but has NO nonce/expiry/chainid and NO EIP-2 malleability guard; same-context re-anchor accepted (idempotent)
replay.evidence: valid anchor ok=true; identical re-submission also ok=true. No replay primitive; changeOwner path is a direct owner call (no signature to replay).

identity_theft.mechanism: address-bound identifier; controller transfer only via owner-authorised changeOwner (no token/approval surface)
identity_theft.evidence: changeOwner by owner ok=true; identityOwner now 0x90F79bf6EB2c4f870365E785982E1f101E93b906. Stolen owner key can seize; no passive transfer surface.

sybil.mechanism: ERC-1056 side: every address is an implicit identity; no issuer gating; near-zero creation cost (~52k first attribute write)
sybil.evidence: attacker created 5/5 independent identities unchallenged. Safety-critical CLAIMS still need a trusted issuer signature, but base identities are free/permissionless.

recovery.mechanism: no recovery primitive; changeOwner requires the current owner key
recovery.evidence: compromised owner key = permanent loss (the hybrid adds on-chain claims but no key recovery).

privacy.mechanism: ERC-1056 attributes are event-only (no storage); but ERC-735 claim `data` is stored and readable via getClaim — unhashed, app-dependent
privacy.evidence: getClaim(...).data read back plaintext "1HGBH41JXMN109186" (the benchmark/app placed the VIN in claim data). No forced hashing; privacy depends on the app hashing/encrypting claim payloads.
